overview:
Grace Meng, a Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a New York City district that leans Democratic by about six points. She has raised over two million dollars and holds more than a million on hand, while Republican Joseph Chou has raised under three thousand dollars with no outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put her chances of winning at roughly ninety-five percent.

The expected margin is about twenty points, matching the district's fundamentals plus the advantages of incumbency and money. With thin direct evidence, uncertainty is somewhat elevated, but every available signal points to a comfortable Meng victory.
